headline: Custom Tile Shower Mistakes to Avoid Before You Sign a Remodeling Contract
articleBody:
Investing in a custom tile shower should add lasting beauty and value to your home. However, cutting corners on the concealed layers underneath leads to water intrusion and structural damage.

Common Mistakes to Avoid
- Assuming tile and grout are waterproof: Grout and tile absorb moisture. Always demand a continuous, approved waterproof membrane installed beneath the tile layer.
- Using standard drywall in wet areas: Ordinary drywall breaks down when exposed to moisture. Use approved cementitious backer units or waterproof foam backer boards.
- Creating flat or reverse floor slopes: Shower floors must maintain a slope of roughly one-quarter inch per foot toward the drain. Verify slope before tiling begins.
- Overlooking transitions, niches, and curbs: Gaps in waterproofing where benches, walls, and curbs meet are prime failure points. Ensure all corners receive continuous sealing.
- Skipping the flood test: Tiling before conducting a 24-hour flood test leaves pan defects undetected. Always insist on water testing the pan before laying floor tile.
